title: Shadow amplification caused KV-cache churn and autoscaler oscillation
creator: Nikhil Rao
summary: A targeted A/B rollout that enabled shadow duplication for a new ranking model produced amplified request traffic to canary instances. The amplification caused frequent KV cache evictions, spiky tail latency, and autoscaler oscillation between scale-up and scale-down states. This ticket captures the postmortem, runbook changes, and prioritized follow-ups to remove amplification risk and harden rollouts.
impact: Approximately 9 minutes of elevated tail latency and 5xxs on canary routes; 5 customers experienced degraded response times, one onboarding trial failed, and a support escalation required manual mitigation.
root_cause_summary: Shadow duplication rate was configured at 1.8x due to a misinterpreted percent multiplier in the rollout spec. Combined with an aggressive per-instance prefetching change, this multiplied request concurrency on canary nodes, causing KV cache thrash and triggering autoscaler hysteresis to oscillate. Lack of a shadow rate limiter and insufficient pre-deploy simulation allowed the bad config to reach production.
telemetry_findings: Shadow duplication multiplier set to 180% (should have been capped at 100%)
KV cache eviction rate spiked 12x on canary instances during the event
Request concurrency per instance exceeded predicted P95 by 3x causing long queueing
Autoscaler scaled up then scaled down repeatedly due to short CPU spikes and long tail latency not included in scale decisions
steps_taken: Emergency: Disabled shadow duplication for the affected rollout via Console
Throttled canary traffic to 10% of original while stabilizing autoscaler policies
Pinned canary nodes to their stable kernel to avoid the prefetch change until investigation completes
Opened a live triage channel and created a temporary dashboard tracking shadow amplification ratio, kv_evictions, instance_concurrency, and autoscaler_events
short_term_mitigations: Add an immediate guard to cap shadow duplication multiplier to 100% in the control plane
Deploy an emergency autoscaler tweak to use a longer evaluation window before scale-down
Revert prefetching change on canaries pending full KV-cache stress test
proposed_safety_changes: Introduce explicit shadow-rate controls in rollout specs with safe defaults
Require shadow amplification simulation in CI that validates KV cache hit-rate and eviction behaviour
Add a canary autoscaler policy that considers queue-length and tail-latency signals in addition to CPU
Implement per-route resource impact estimation in the console before enabling duplication
Enforce rollout linting that rejects multipliers expressed as percentages >100
runbook_updates: New section: Shadow duplication emergency procedures (how to disable, safe verification steps)
Playbook: KV cache thrash containment (staged pinning, graceful eviction commands, and verification)
Checklist: Pre-rollout simulation steps including shadow-sim with kv-cache pressure profile
Operator steps: When to apply autoscaler hysteresis overrides and how to revert them safely
